title: Proof: what a REAL Ctrl-Cmd-D does in cmux on a Mac with default settings (and a real Cmd-D as the control)
why: STATUS 1649, cmux-ad 14:50Z: in the real-key smoke round a real Ctrl-Cmd-D made no New Column, while debug.key Ctrl-Cmd-D passed 10/10; very likely macOS's system hotkey 70 'Look up in Dictionary' (Ctrl-Cmd-D, on by default) takes the key before cmux. This journey records, for a real Cmd-D (control) and then a real Ctrl-Cmd-D: whether cmux's key router saw the key at all, which action ran (the app's action log), which other apps' windows are on screen (a Look Up panel), and a full-display screenshot right after the key. Needs a whole-host lease on a CuaDriver-granted mini.
